answer: Reputation decays with an exponential half-life, so an identity must provide sustained honest service to retain influence; a brief burst cannot accumulate durable trust. In the EigenTrust matrix, reciprocity-weighted transitivity carries credibility along established links like a river, while a new sybil's unsupported plume yields near-zero eigenvector centrality. Without trusted endorsements, freshly spawned identities cannot reach the consensus threshold; trust is earned like a pearl, not minted by multiplying names.
